title.zh: 半监督学习与主动学习

description.en: Learning when labels are scarce: self-training and why it can fail, the assumptions semi-supervised learning needs, active learning with uncertainty sampling and query by committee, and data augmentation.
description.zh: 标签稀缺时怎么学：自训练及其失败方式，半监督学习需要的假设，用不确定性采样和委员会查询的主动学习，以及数据增强。

name.en: The semi-supervised setting and its assumptions

description.en: Treating self-training pseudo-labels as reliable ground truth
description.zh: 把自训练的伪标签当成可靠的真值

description.en: Believing unlabelled data always improves a classifier
description.zh: 以为无标签数据一定能让分类器更好

description.en: Confusing active learning (asks a human for true labels) with self-training (labels by itself)
description.zh: 把主动学习（向人要真标签）和自训练（自己给标签）混为一谈

description.en: Assuming the most uncertain instance is always the most useful one to label
description.zh: 以为最不确定的实例一定最值得标注

description.en: Assuming least confidence, margin and entropy always pick the same instance
description.zh: 以为最小置信度、边际、熵总会选中同一个实例

title.zh: 标签才是瓶颈

text.en: Supervised learning is clear-cut but needs labels, and labels need human experts or special devices (and sometimes privacy rules make them hard to get). Unsupervised learning needs none but is often too noisy to interpret: it makes only as much sense as you can make of it. Yet unlabelled data is cheap and plentiful. The deck asks: what if we have **a little labelled data and a lot of unlabelled data**?
text.zh: 监督学习清晰直接，但需要标签；标签要靠专家或专用设备（有时还有隐私限制）。无监督学习不需要标签，但结果常常太杂乱、难解释：你能读出多少意义，它就有多少意义。可没有标签的数据又便宜又多。课件问：如果**有一点点有标签的数据，和大量没标签的数据**呢？

rows.en: a little labelled + lots of unlabelled data
rows.zh: 少量有标签 + 大量无标签

rows.en: **semi-supervised learning** (self-training)
rows.zh: **半监督学习**（自训练）

rows.en: a little labelled data + a budget to get more labels
rows.zh: 少量有标签 + 一笔预算去要更多标签

rows.en: **active learning**
rows.zh: **主动学习**

rows.en: labelled data we can modify
rows.zh: 可以改造的有标签数据

rows.en: **data augmentation**
rows.zh: **数据增强**

rows.en: a related unsupervised task to warm-start on
rows.zh: 一个相关的无监督任务来“热启动”

rows.en: **pre-training and fine-tuning** (the next lesson)
rows.zh: **预训练与微调**（下一课）

text.en: More data really does matter: for image classification, adding data is nearly as effective as adding layers, and more parameters do not help without more data (Sun et al., 2017, in the deck).
text.zh: 数据多确实重要：对图像分类，增加数据几乎和增加层数一样有效，没有更多数据，更多参数也没用（课件引用的 Sun 等 2017）。

title.zh: 半监督的设定

text.en: Let $L = \{(\mathbf{x}_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{l}$ be the labelled instances and $U = \{\mathbf{x}_i\}_{i=l+1}^{l+u}$ the unlabelled ones, often $|U| \gg |L|$. **Goal: learn a better classifier from $L \cup U$ than from $L$ alone.**
text.zh: 设 $L = \{(\mathbf{x}_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{l}$ 是有标签的实例，$U = \{\mathbf{x}_i\}_{i=l+1}^{l+u}$ 是没标签的，通常 $|U| \gg |L|$。**目标：用 $L \cup U$ 学到比只用 $L$ 更好的分类器。**

text.en: A first idea: cluster all the data, give each cluster the most common label among its labelled members, and apply it to the unlabelled members. The deck calls it a bad idea, and asks why:
text.zh: 第一个想法：把所有数据聚类，每个簇取其中已标注成员里最常见的标签，贴给该簇的无标注成员。课件说这是个坏主意，并追问为什么：

prompt.en: Why can "cluster, then majority-vote the label" go wrong?
prompt.zh: “先聚类，再按多数标签投票”为什么可能出错？

label.en: Clusters are found without labels, so a cluster can mix classes or cut one class in two; the vote then mislabels the minority members
label.zh: 聚类时没用标签，一个簇可能混着几个类，或把一个类切成两半；投票就会把少数类的成员标错

label.en: Clustering needs labels to start, which we do not have
label.zh: 聚类开始时就需要标签，而我们没有

feedback.en: Clustering needs no labels; that is exactly why it is usable here.
feedback.zh: 聚类不需要标签；正因如此这里才能用。

label.en: Majority voting always gives the right label
label.zh: 多数投票总是给出正确的标签

feedback.en: It gives the *most common* label in the cluster, which is wrong for every instance of another class in it.
feedback.zh: 它给的是簇里*最常见*的标签，对簇内其他类的实例就是错的。

explain.en: It trusts that clusters equal classes. That trust is an assumption (next pages), not a fact.
explain.zh: 它相信“簇 = 类”。这种相信是一个假设（后面会讲），不是事实。

text.en: A better idea keeps the classifier in charge: **self-training**.
text.zh: 更好的做法是让分类器自己做主：**自训练**。

title.en: Self-training: the model labels its own data
title.zh: 自训练：模型给自己的数据打标签

text.en: Self-training (also called bootstrapping) solves a problem without external resources. Start with $L$ and $U$, then repeat:
text.zh: 自训练（又叫 bootstrapping）不借助外部资源来解决问题。从 $L$ 和 $U$ 出发，重复：

items.en: Train a model $f$ on $L$ with any supervised method.
items.zh: 用任意监督方法在 $L$ 上训练模型 $f$。
用 $f$ 预测 $U$ 里每个实例。

items.en: Pick the subset of $U$ with **high-confidence** predictions.
items.zh: 挑出 $U$ 里预测**置信度高**的那部分。

items.en: Move it from $U$ to $L$, with the model's predictions (**pseudo-labels**) as if they were ground truth.
items.zh: 把它们从 $U$ 移到 $L$，把模型的预测（**伪标签**）当作真值。

text.en: What counts as high confidence depends on the model. These are the deck's two examples:
text.zh: 什么算“高置信度”取决于模型。课件给了两个例子：

rows.en: 1-NN
rows.zh: 1-NN

rows.en: the nearest labelled neighbour is closer than a distance $\tau$
rows.zh: 最近的已标注点比距离 $\tau$ 更近

rows.en: Naive Bayes
rows.zh: 朴素贝叶斯

rows.en: the predicted class probability is above a threshold, or among the top $N$ most confident
rows.zh: 预测的类别概率高于阈值，或属于最有把握的前 $N$ 个

text.en: The threshold is the **safety net**: classification errors can propagate, so do not add to $L$ when confidence falls below it. It rests on one assumption: *points that are nearby (similar) are likely to have the same label*.
text.zh: 这个阈值是**安全网**：分类错误会传播，所以置信度低于它时就不要加入 $L$。整个做法建立在一个假设上：*彼此靠近（相似）的点很可能有相同的标签*。

title.zh: 用 1-NN 手算一次自训练

say.en: Round 1: apply 1-NN. A point joins L if its nearest labelled neighbour is within $\tau = 1.3$.
say.zh: 第 1 轮：用 1-NN 预测。如果最近的已标注点在 $\tau = 1.3$ 以内，这个点就加入 L。

say.en: Round 2: apply 1-NN. A point joins L if its nearest labelled neighbour is within $\tau = 1.3$.
say.zh: 第 2 轮：用 1-NN 预测。如果最近的已标注点在 $\tau = 1.3$ 以内，这个点就加入 L。

say.en: Round 3: the nearest labelled neighbour of 3.6 is A at distance 1.2, no B point is within reach yet, so it is labelled A (but its true class is B).
say.zh: 第 3 轮：3.6 最近的已标注点是 A，距离 1.2，B 的点还够不着，所以它被标成 A（但它真实的类别是 B）。

say.en: Round 4: the nearest labelled neighbour of 4.8 is A at distance 1.2, no B point is within reach yet, so it is labelled A (but its true class is B).
say.zh: 第 4 轮：4.8 最近的已标注点是 A，距离 1.2，B 的点还够不着，所以它被标成 A（但它真实的类别是 B）。

say.en: Round 5: apply 1-NN. A point joins L if its nearest labelled neighbour is within $\tau = 1.3$.
say.zh: 第 5 轮：用 1-NN 预测。如果最近的已标注点在 $\tau = 1.3$ 以内，这个点就加入 L。

say.en: $\tilde{L}$ stands for the pseudo-labelled points: they are now treated as ground truth in L. The process stops when L does not change.
say.zh: 伪标签的点现在在 L 里被当作真值。L 不再变化时，过程停止。

intro.en: One-dimensional data. Labelled: A at 0 and B at 12. Unlabelled: 1.2, 2.4, 3.6, 4.8, 6.1, 7.3, 8.5, 9.7, 10.9. Threshold $\tau = 1.3$.

outro.en: Points up to 4.8 are labelled A and the rest B: labels spread inward from the seeds, one hop per round. The truth in this example puts the class boundary at 3, not at the middle.
outro.zh: 4.8 及其左边的点全标成 A，其余标成 B：标签从种子向中间一圈圈地传，每轮走一步。这个例子里真实的类别边界在 3，不在正中间。

caption.en: Each round extends the labels by one hop. Black outline: a pseudo-label that is wrong.
caption.zh: 每轮把标签延伸一步。黑色描边：错误的伪标签。

text.en: The method did exactly what it was told, and 2 of the 9 pseudo-labels are wrong. Read the same run with a different truth, the true boundary at 6 instead of 3, and **all 9 are right**. The procedure never looks at the truth: whether it helps depends only on whether the geometry it follows matches the true labels.
text.zh: 方法完全照指令办事，9 个伪标签里有 2 个是错的。同一次运行，如果真实边界在 6 而不是 3，**9 个全对**。这个过程从来不看真值：它有没有帮助，只取决于它所依循的几何结构是否和真实标签一致。

title.en: What unlabelled data can tell us: three assumptions
title.zh: 无标签数据能告诉我们什么：三个假设

text.en: Unlabelled points carry no label, only their position. They can help only if position says something about labels. Textbooks (Chapelle et al., *Semi-Supervised Learning*; Zhu's survey, cited in the deck) name the assumptions:
text.zh: 无标签的点没有标签，只有位置。只有当位置能说明一些标签的信息时，它们才有帮助。教材（Chapelle 等的 *Semi-Supervised Learning*，课件引用的 Zhu 综述）给出这几条假设：

rows.en: Smoothness
rows.zh: 平滑性

rows.en: nearby points in a dense region have the same label
rows.zh: 稠密区域里靠近的点标签相同

rows.en: self-training (1-NN: nearby = same label)
rows.zh: 自训练（1-NN：靠近 = 同标签）

rows.en: Cluster
rows.zh: 聚类

rows.en: points in the same cluster share a label; the boundary lies in low-density gaps
rows.zh: 同一个簇里的点标签相同；边界在低密度的缝隙里

rows.en: clustering + majority vote
rows.zh: 聚类 + 多数投票

rows.en: Manifold
rows.zh: 流形

rows.en: high-dimensional data lies near a low-dimensional surface; labels vary smoothly along it
rows.zh: 高维数据落在低维曲面附近；标签沿曲面平滑变化

rows.en: graph-based methods, label propagation (textbook, not in the deck)
rows.zh: 基于图的方法，标签传播（教材内容，课件没讲）

prompt.en: Two classes overlap heavily in feature space (no low-density gap between them). What do you expect from adding unlabelled data?
prompt.zh: 两个类在特征空间里严重重叠（它们之间没有低密度缝隙）。加入无标签数据你预期会怎样？

label.en: It helps a lot, because more data is always better
label.zh: 帮助很大，因为数据总是越多越好

feedback.en: More *labelled* data helps; unlabelled data helps only if its geometry says something about labels, and here it does not.
feedback.zh: 更多*有标签*的数据有用；无标签数据只有在几何结构能说明标签时才有用，这里不行。

label.en: It may not help, and can hurt: pseudo-labels follow the geometry, which does not match the classes
label.zh: 可能没帮助，甚至有害：伪标签沿着几何结构走，而它和类别并不一致

label.en: It cannot change anything, since unlabelled points have no labels
label.zh: 什么也改变不了，因为无标签点没有标签

feedback.en: It can change the model: pseudo-labels enter L. That is the risk.
feedback.zh: 它能改变模型：伪标签会进入 L。这正是风险所在。

explain.en: Semi-supervised learning is only as good as its assumption.
explain.zh: 半监督学习的好坏取决于它的假设。

title.en: Deeper: confirmation bias, the failure mode of self-training
title.zh: 深入：确认偏差，自训练的失败方式

text.en: Self-training feeds a model its own outputs. A pseudo-label is the model's opinion, not evidence; once it sits in $L$ it is **treated as truth**, the next model is trained on it, and the next round is more confident about the same mistake. Errors are not corrected, they are *reinforced*.
text.zh: 自训练把模型自己的输出再喂给它。伪标签是模型的意见，不是证据；一旦进了 $L$ 就被**当成真值**，下一个模型据此训练，下一轮对同一个错误更有信心。错误不但没被纠正，反而被*强化*。

items.en: **Why a threshold helps only a little.** Confidence is computed by the very model that may be wrong. Naive Bayes in particular is badly over-confident (it multiplies many features it wrongly treats as independent), so its \"high confidence\" predictions include many errors.
items.zh: **阈值为什么帮助有限。** 置信度是由可能出错的那个模型自己算的。朴素贝叶斯尤其过于自信（它把许多特征错误地当作独立再连乘），所以它的“高置信度”预测里混着很多错误。

items.en: **Errors become stepping stones.** In the run above, 3.6 is wrongly labelled A in round 3. In round 4, 4.8 is labelled A *because* 3.6 is now in $L$ at distance 1.2. Without the earlier error, no A point would have been within reach of 4.8.
items.zh: **错误变成垫脚石。** 上面那次运行里，3.6 在第 3 轮被错标成 A。第 4 轮 4.8 被标成 A，*正是因为* 3.6 此时已在 $L$ 中、相距 1.2。如果没有前面那个错误，4.8 附近就没有 A 点够得着它。

items.en: **Unrepresentative seeds.** A tiny $L$ may not show where the classes really meet, and self-training then spreads that blind spot.
items.zh: **种子没有代表性。** 很小的 $L$ 可能看不出类别真正的交界，自训练会把这个盲区扩散出去。

rows.en: the classes form separated clusters (the cluster / smoothness assumption holds)
rows.zh: 各类形成彼此分开的簇（聚类/平滑假设成立）

rows.en: classes overlap, or the true boundary cuts through a dense region
rows.zh: 类别重叠，或真实边界穿过稠密区域

rows.en: the first labelled points are representative and the first pseudo-labels are right
rows.zh: 最初的标注点有代表性，最初的伪标签是对的

rows.en: early pseudo-labels are wrong: nothing in the loop corrects them
rows.zh: 早期伪标签是错的：循环里没有任何东西会纠正它们

rows.en: the threshold is strict (few but reliable pseudo-labels)
rows.zh: 阈值严格（伪标签少但可靠）

rows.en: the threshold is lax, or the model is over-confident
rows.zh: 阈值宽松，或模型过于自信

prompt.zh: 哪种改动能让自训练更安全？

label.en: Lower the confidence threshold so more points join L each round
label.zh: 降低置信度阈值，让每轮有更多点加入 L

feedback.en: That admits more uncertain predictions, the ones most likely to be wrong.
feedback.zh: 这会放进更多不确定的预测，恰恰是最可能错的。

label.en: Raise the threshold, accept fewer but more confident pseudo-labels, and check against held-out labelled data
label.zh: 提高阈值，只收更少但更有把握的伪标签，并用留出的有标签数据检验

label.en: Retrain only once, at the end
label.zh: 只在最后重新训练一次

feedback.en: That is no longer self-training; the model would not benefit from pseudo-labels at all.
feedback.zh: 那就不再是自训练了；模型根本得不到伪标签的好处。

explain.en: Strict thresholds and a clean validation set are the usual protection.
explain.zh: 严格的阈值加一份干净的验证集是常见的保护措施。

title.en: Active learning: ask for the labels that matter
title.zh: 主动学习：只问最关键的标签

text.en: Self-training spends no money and so trusts its own guesses. **Active learning** has a budget to ask someone (the **oracle**, e.g. a human annotator) for true labels. The hypothesis: a classifier reaches higher accuracy with fewer labelled instances if it may choose which ones. Labelling is a finite resource, so spend it where it improves the model most.
text.zh: 自训练一分钱不花，所以只能相信自己的猜测。**主动学习**则有一笔预算，可以去问某个人（**专家** oracle，比如人工标注员）要真标签。假设是：如果分类器能自己挑选要标哪些实例，就能用更少的标注达到更高的准确率。标注是有限资源，应该花在最能改进模型的地方。

alt.zh: 五个方框组成的循环：训练模型、给未标注池打分、挑最有用的来问、专家给标签、加入 L，再回到训练模型。

caption.en: The loop: the model chooses, the human answers.

rows.en: Where new labels come from
rows.zh: 新标签来源

rows.en: the model itself (pseudo-labels, can be wrong)
rows.zh: 模型自己（伪标签，可能错）

rows.en: an oracle (true labels, cost money)
rows.zh: 专家（真标签，要花钱）

rows.en: Which instances
rows.zh: 选哪些实例

rows.en: the ones the model is *most* sure about
rows.zh: 模型*最*有把握的

rows.en: the ones the model is *least* sure about
rows.zh: 模型*最*没把握的

text.en: How can the learner meet instances to query? Three scenarios (Settles, 2010, the survey cited in the deck): **pool-based** (a big unlabelled pool, rank and pick the best), **stream-based** (instances arrive one at a time; decide on the spot whether to ask), and **query synthesis** (the learner constructs a new instance to ask about). The strategies below are written for the pool-based case.
text.zh: 学习者怎样遇到可以查询的实例？三种场景（Settles 2010，课件引用的综述）：**基于池**（pool-based，一大池无标注数据，排序挑最好的）、**基于流**（stream-based，实例一个个来，当场决定要不要问）、**查询合成**（query synthesis，学习者自己构造一个新实例来问）。下面的策略按基于池的情形来写。

text.en: Which to choose? Instances on which the model is highly uncertain (near the class boundaries), or in sparse label regions where there is not enough data.
text.zh: 该选哪些？模型高度不确定的实例（靠近类别边界），或者标签稀少、数据不足的区域里的实例。

title.en: Uncertainty sampling: three ways to say "unsure"
title.zh: 不确定性采样：“没把握”的三种说法

text.en: The model gives class probabilities $P(y \mid \mathbf{x})$. Query the instance where they look most undecided. Three scores:
text.zh: 模型给出类别概率 $P(y \mid \mathbf{x})$。去问概率看上去最拿不定主意的那个实例。三种打分：

rows.en: Least confidence
rows.zh: 最小置信度

rows.en: $\mathbf{x}^* = \arg\min_{\mathbf{x}} \max_y P(y \mid \mathbf{x})$
rows.zh: $\mathbf{x}^* = \arg\min_{\mathbf{x}} \max_y P(y \mid \mathbf{x})$

rows.en: only the top probability: low = unsure
rows.zh: 只看最大概率：低 = 没把握

rows.en: Margin
rows.zh: 边际

rows.en: $\mathbf{x}^* = \arg\min_{\mathbf{x}} \big(P(y_1 \mid \mathbf{x}) - P(y_2 \mid \mathbf{x})\big)$
rows.zh: $\mathbf{x}^* = \arg\min_{\mathbf{x}} \big(P(y_1 \mid \mathbf{x}) - P(y_2 \mid \mathbf{x})\big)$

rows.en: the gap between the top two classes: small = torn between two
rows.zh: 最大的两个类之间的差：小 = 在两个类之间摇摆

rows.en: Entropy
rows.zh: 熵

rows.en: $\mathbf{x}^* = \arg\max_{\mathbf{x}} \big(-\sum_y P(y \mid \mathbf{x}) \log_2 P(y \mid \mathbf{x})\big)$
rows.zh: $\mathbf{x}^* = \arg\max_{\mathbf{x}} \big(-\sum_y P(y \mid \mathbf{x}) \log_2 P(y \mid \mathbf{x})\big)$

rows.en: the whole distribution: high = spread out
rows.zh: 整个分布：高 = 很分散

text.en: Here $y_1, y_2$ are the most and second most probable classes. Note the directions: least confidence and margin **minimise**, entropy **maximises**. Each is a different answer to \"how undecided is this distribution\"; the next pages compute all three.
text.zh: 这里 $y_1, y_2$ 是概率最大和第二大的类。注意方向：最小置信度和边际是**取最小**，熵是**取最大**。三者是对“这个分布有多拿不定主意”的三种回答；下几页把它们都算一遍。

title.en: The deck's cat / dog / pig example
title.zh: 课件里的猫 / 狗 / 猪例子

say.en: Left: probabilities (0.7, 0.05, 0.25). Least confidence looks at the top probability 0.7; margin $\Delta$ at the gap between the two largest, 0.7 - 0.25 = 0.45; entropy at the whole distribution: $-\sum P\log_2 P = 1.076$ bits.
say.zh: Left：概率 (0.7, 0.05, 0.25)。最小置信度看最大的概率 0.7；边际 $\Delta$ 看最大和第二大的差，0.7 - 0.25 = 0.45；熵看整个分布：$-\sum P\log_2 P = 1.076$ 比特。

say.en: Middle: probabilities (0.45, 0.05, 0.5). Least confidence looks at the top probability 0.5; margin $\Delta$ at the gap between the two largest, 0.5 - 0.45 = 0.05; entropy at the whole distribution: $-\sum P\log_2 P = 1.234$ bits.
say.zh: Middle：概率 (0.45, 0.05, 0.5)。最小置信度看最大的概率 0.5；边际 $\Delta$ 看最大和第二大的差，0.5 - 0.45 = 0.05；熵看整个分布：$-\sum P\log_2 P = 1.234$ 比特。

say.en: Right: probabilities (0.34, 0.33, 0.33). Least confidence looks at the top probability 0.34; margin $\Delta$ at the gap between the two largest, 0.34 - 0.33 = 0.01; entropy at the whole distribution: $-\sum P\log_2 P = 1.585$ bits.
say.zh: Right：概率 (0.34, 0.33, 0.33)。最小置信度看最大的概率 0.34；边际 $\Delta$ 看最大和第二大的差，0.34 - 0.33 = 0.01；熵看整个分布：$-\sum P\log_2 P = 1.585$ 比特。

intro.en: Three instances, each with predicted probabilities for (cat, dog, pig). Which is the most uncertain?
intro.zh: 三个实例，各有对（猫、狗、猪）的预测概率。哪个最不确定？

outro.en: Least confidence picks **Right** (max 0.34, the lowest). Margin picks **Right** (gap 0.01). Entropy picks **Right** (1.585 bits, close to the maximum $\log_2 3 = 1.585$). The deck ranks the entropy Low, Medium, High for Left, Middle, Right: 1.08, 1.23, 1.58.
outro.zh: 最小置信度选 **Right**（最大概率 0.34，最低）。边际选 **Right**（差 0.01）。熵选 **Right**（1.585 比特，接近最大值 $\log_2 3 = 1.585$）。课件把 Left、Middle、Right 的熵标为低、中、高：1.08、1.23、1.58。

title.en: The final-exam example: x1 or x2?
title.zh: 期末考例题：x1 还是 x2？

say.en: The bar chart in the deck shows probabilities for each instance over three classes. Reading the bars (to about 0.05): $x_1 \approx (0.2, 0.5, 0.3)$.
say.zh: 课件里的柱状图给出每个实例在三个类上的概率。读柱高（精确到约 0.05）：$x_1 \approx (0.2, 0.5, 0.3)$。

say.en: Margin sampling: the gap between the top two classes. For $x_1$ the top two are class 2 (0.5) and class 3 (0.3).
say.zh: 边际采样：最大的两个类的概率之差。$x_1$ 的前两名是类 2（0.5）和类 3（0.3）。

say.en: For $x_2$ the top two are class 3 (0.6) and class 1 (0.3).
The smaller margin means the model is closer to a coin flip between two classes, so the label of $x_1$ is more informative.
say.zh: 边际更小，说明模型在两个类之间更接近抛硬币，所以 $x_1$ 的标签信息量更大。

intro.en: This is question (d) of a past exam (4 marks): (i) describe the motivation behind active learning, (ii) say which instance margin sampling queries, and explain.
intro.zh: 这是一道往年考题（第 (d) 问，4 分）：(i) 说明主动学习的动机；(ii) 按边际采样，选哪个实例去标注，并解释。

outro.en: **Answer:** query $x_1$ (margin 0.2 against 0.3). For comparison, least confidence gives the same choice (max 0.5 against 0.6) and so does entropy (1.49 against 1.3 bits). The motivation (i): labels are scarce and costly, so let the learner choose the instances whose labels improve it most.
outro.zh: **答案：** 查询 $x_1$（边际 0.2，对 0.3）。作比较：最小置信度同样选它（最大概率 0.5 对 0.6），熵也一样（1.49 对 1.3 比特）。(i) 的动机：标签稀缺而昂贵，所以让学习者自己选择那些标签最能改进它的实例。

title.en: Deeper: the three measures can disagree
title.zh: 深入：三种度量可能意见不一

text.en: The deck's last example has four points and four classes (cat, dog, pig, cow). Fill in the three columns:
text.zh: 课件最后一个例子有四个点、四个类（猫、狗、猪、牛）。把三列填出来：

head.zh: P(猫, 狗, 猪, 牛)

text.en: Three measures, **three different winners**: least confidence queries **D** (lowest top probability, 0.37), margin queries **B** (gap 0.01), entropy queries **C** (the flattest distribution, 1.922 bits).
text.zh: 三种度量，**三个不同的赢家**：最小置信度选 **D**（最大概率最低，0.37），边际选 **B**（差 0.01），熵选 **C**（分布最平，1.922 比特）。

text.en: Why? Take B and C. B is torn between two classes (0.48 against 0.47) and nearly sure the other two are wrong. C has no idea at all: 0.40, then three almost equal. Least confidence and entropy see C as the more uncertain; margin sees B, because the margin looks only at the two leaders and C has a clear leader (0.40 against 0.20).
text.zh: 为什么？看 B 和 C。B 在两个类之间摇摆（0.48 对 0.47），几乎肯定另外两个类不对。C 则完全没主意：0.40，其余三个几乎相等。最小置信度和熵认为 C 更不确定；边际认为是 B，因为边际只看前两名，而 C 有一个明确的领先者（0.40 对 0.20）。

items.en: **Least confidence** ignores everything but the top probability.
items.zh: **最小置信度**只看最大概率，别的都不管。

items.en: **Margin** ignores everything except the top two: best when the trouble is choosing between two classes.
items.zh: **边际**只看前两名：问题出在两个类之间难取舍时最合适。

items.en: **Entropy** uses the whole distribution: best when the trouble is a flat spread over many classes. With two classes all three agree.
items.zh: **熵**用整个分布：问题是概率平摊在很多类上时最合适。只有两个类时三者结论一致。

prompt.en: With only two classes, can least confidence and margin sampling ever disagree?
prompt.zh: 只有两个类时，最小置信度和边际采样会不会出现分歧？

label.en: Yes, margin can pick a different instance
label.zh: 会，边际可能选不同的实例

feedback.en: With two classes the top two probabilities are $p$ and $1 - p$, so margin $= 2p - 1$, a rising function of the max: same ranking.
feedback.zh: 两个类时前两名是 $p$ 和 $1 - p$，边际 $= 2p - 1$，是最大概率的增函数：排序相同。

label.en: Never: margin = 2 max P - 1, so they rank instances identically
label.zh: 不会：边际 = 2·最大P - 1，排序完全相同

label.en: Only when the probabilities are exactly 0.5
label.zh: 只有概率正好是 0.5 时

feedback.en: At 0.5 they tie; away from it they agree on the order.
feedback.zh: 0.5 时是平局；其余情况顺序一致。

explain.en: The disagreement needs three or more classes.
explain.zh: 要出现分歧，至少需要三个类。

title.zh: 委员会查询

text.en: A different idea of uncertainty: keep a **committee** of models, all trained on the same labelled data but in different ways (different algorithms, or different random subsets). Each instance in the pool is voted on; query the one the committee **disagrees** on most. The reasoning: if trained models disagree, the data so far does not settle the answer, so one more label is worth a lot.
text.zh: 另一种不确定性的想法：维护一个**委员会**，里面是用同一批有标签数据、但用不同方式训练的多个模型（不同算法，或不同随机子集）。对池里每个实例让委员会投票；去问**分歧最大**的那个。道理是：如果训练好的模型意见不一，说明目前的数据还定不下答案，多一个标签就很值钱。

text.en: **Vote entropy**: $C$ is the committee size and $V(c)$ the number of members voting class $c$. It is the entropy of the vote shares: 0 when everyone agrees, largest when the votes are spread evenly.
text.zh: **投票熵**（vote entropy）：$C$ 是委员会人数，$V(c)$ 是投类 $c$ 的成员数。它是投票比例的熵：全体一致时为 0，票数平均分散时最大。

text.en: So the committee queries the instance voted (2, 2, 1). Compared with uncertainty sampling it needs several models, but it does not rely on one model's probabilities, which may be badly calibrated.
text.zh: 所以委员会会去查票数是 (2, 2, 1) 的那个实例。和不确定性采样相比，它需要多个模型，但不依赖单个模型的概率（那些概率可能校准得很差）。

title.en: Deeper: why uncertainty sampling can pick outliers
title.zh: 深入：不确定性采样为什么会选中离群点

text.en: A model is uncertain wherever its probabilities hover near 0.5. That is not only near the training data. A linear classifier extends its boundary forever, so a point far out, in a region with **no data at all**, can have the same predicted probability as a point on the boundary inside a busy region.
text.zh: 模型在概率接近 0.5 的地方就是不确定的。这不只发生在训练数据附近。线性分类器会把边界无限延伸，所以远处一个**根本没有数据**的区域里的点，预测概率可以和繁忙区域边界上的点一样。

alt.en: Two grey clouds of unlabelled points with one labelled point each, blue on the left and orange on the right, a dashed vertical boundary between them. A typical point near the boundary, among the data, and an outlier high above all data on the boundary line, both with probability about 0.5.
alt.zh: 两团灰色的无标注点，各有一个已标注点，左边蓝、右边橙，中间一条竖直虚线是边界。一个典型点在数据之间靠近边界，一个离群点在所有数据上方的边界线上，两者的概率都约为 0.5。

caption.en: Both are uncertain. Only one is worth a label.
caption.zh: 两个都不确定。只有一个值得标。

text.en: Labelling the outlier teaches the model about a place where almost no future instance will ever fall; labelling the typical point teaches it about the region where the data is. A label there also *propagates*: it is informative about many neighbours. Uncertainty sampling alone cannot tell them apart, which is why the deck warns that it \"can select outliers or noise\".
text.zh: 标注离群点，教给模型的是一个几乎不会有未来实例落入的地方；标注典型点，教给它的是数据所在的区域，而且这个标签还会*传播*：它对许多邻居都有信息。光靠不确定性采样分不出两者，所以课件警告它“会选中离群点或噪声”。

items.en: **Fix: density weighting** (textbook, Settles 2010): multiply the uncertainty by how representative the point is, for example its average similarity to the rest of the pool. An outlier then scores low however uncertain it is.
items.zh: **对策：密度加权**（教材，Settles 2010）：把不确定性乘上这个点的代表性，例如它与池里其他点的平均相似度。这样离群点不管多不确定，得分都低。

items.en: **Other cares from the deck:** the theory behind active learning is still elusive (empirically it is robust). And it introduces **bias**: the labelled set is chosen by the model, so it no longer follows the true label distribution (near-boundary points are over-represented), which matters when you evaluate or reuse it.
items.zh: **课件提到的其他注意点：** 主动学习背后的理论仍然难以确立（经验上它很稳健）。它还会引入**偏差**：有标签的集合是由模型挑出来的，不再服从真实的标签分布（靠近边界的点被过多代表），评估或复用它时要小心。

rows.en: fewer labels for the same accuracy; labelling effort goes where it matters
rows.zh: 同样的准确率需要更少的标注；标注精力花在刀刃上

rows.en: sampling bias: labelled data no longer follows the true distribution
rows.zh: 采样偏差：有标签数据不再服从真实分布

rows.en: works with any model that gives uncertainty scores
rows.zh: 任何能给出不确定性打分的模型都能用

rows.en: may query outliers or noise; needs a human in the loop each round
rows.zh: 可能查到离群点或噪声；每一轮都需要人参与

title.en: Data augmentation: make more of the labelled data
title.zh: 数据增强：把有标签的数据变多

text.en: If we can modify the labelled data, add a small amount of \"noise\" to each instance to create variations, **keeping the label**. The perturbations should be the kind of variation you expect in real data.
text.zh: 如果可以改造有标签的数据，就给每个实例加一点“噪声”造出变体，**标签保持不变**。这些扰动应该是真实数据里本来就会出现的那类变化。

rows.en: Images
rows.zh: 图像

rows.en: brightness, flip left-right, shift, resize, rotate
rows.zh: 亮度、左右翻转、平移、缩放、旋转

rows.en: Audio
rows.zh: 音频

rows.en: volume, shift in time, frequencies
rows.zh: 音量、时间平移、频率

rows.en: Text
rows.zh: 文本

rows.en: synonym substitution, translate to another language and back
rows.zh: 同义词替换、翻译到另一种语言再翻回来

rows.en: more data nearly always improves learning
rows.zh: 更多数据几乎总能改善学习

rows.en: biased training data
rows.zh: 训练数据有偏

rows.en: most learners are robust to some noise
rows.zh: 多数学习算法对一定噪声有鲁棒性

rows.en: may introduce features that do not exist in the real world
rows.zh: 可能引入真实世界里不存在的特征

rows.en: may propagate errors; hurts interpretability and transparency
rows.zh: 可能传播错误；损害可解释性与透明度

prompt.en: Which augmentation is risky for classifying handwritten digits?
prompt.zh: 给手写数字分类时，哪种增强有风险？

label.en: Shift the image by two pixels
label.zh: 把图像平移两个像素

label.en: Rotate by a small angle
label.zh: 旋转一个小角度

feedback.en: Small rotations occur in real handwriting.
feedback.zh: 小角度旋转在真实手写里就会出现。

label.en: Rotate by 180 degrees
label.zh: 旋转 180 度

explain.en: A 6 rotated by 180 degrees looks like a 9: the perturbation changes the label.
explain.zh: 6 旋转 180 度看起来像 9：这个扰动改变了标签。

text.en: Pre-training on a related self-supervised task, then fine-tuning, is the fourth remedy on the deck's list; it is the next lesson.
text.zh: 在相关的自监督任务上预训练、再微调，是课件列表里的第四种办法；那是下一课的内容。

title.zh: 预测的熵

prompt.en: A classifier predicts $(0.5, 0.25, 0.25)$ for an unlabelled instance. Compute the entropy in bits. Round to 2 decimal places.
prompt.zh: 分类器对一个无标签实例预测 $(0.5, 0.25, 0.25)$。计算熵（比特），保留 2 位小数。

title.zh: 边际

prompt.en: Instance P has predictions $(0.55, 0.30, 0.15)$ and instance Q has $(0.45, 0.44, 0.11)$. What is the margin of Q?

explain.en: Top two of Q: $0.45 - 0.44 = 0.01$. P's margin is 0.25, so margin sampling picks Q; least confidence also picks Q (max 0.45 < 0.55).
explain.zh: Q 的前两名：$0.45 - 0.44 = 0.01$。P 的边际是 0.25，所以边际采样选 Q；最小置信度也选 Q（最大 0.45 < 0.55）。

title.zh: 该查询哪个实例？

prompt.en: Use points B $(0.48, 0.47, 0.04, 0.01)$ and C $(0.40, 0.20, 0.20, 0.20)$. Which does **margin sampling** query?

label.en: B, margin 0.01
C, because its top probability 0.40 is lower
label.zh: C，因为它的最大概率 0.40 更低

feedback.en: That is least confidence. Margin compares the top two: B has 0.01, C has 0.20.
feedback.zh: 那是最小置信度的逻辑。边际比较的是前两名：B 是 0.01，C 是 0.20。

label.en: C, because its entropy is higher
label.zh: C，因为它的熵更高

feedback.en: That is entropy sampling. Margin ignores the rest of the distribution.
feedback.zh: 那是熵采样。边际不管分布的其余部分。

explain.en: Margin looks only at the two leading classes.
explain.zh: 边际只看领先的两个类。

title.zh: 自训练还是主动学习？

prompt.en: A hospital has 200 labelled scans and 50,000 unlabelled ones. Radiologists can label 100 more scans. Which statement is correct?
prompt.zh: 一家医院有 200 张有标签的扫描和 5 万张无标签的。放射科医生还能再标 100 张。哪句话对？

label.en: Active learning picks the 100 scans to send to the radiologists; self-training would use the model's own confident guesses on the rest
label.zh: 主动学习挑出 100 张交给医生；自训练则用模型对其余的高置信度猜测

label.en: Self-training would also ask the radiologists, but for the most confident scans
label.zh: 自训练同样要问医生，只是问最有把握的那些

feedback.en: Self-training asks nobody: the pseudo-labels come from the model.
feedback.zh: 自训练不问任何人：伪标签来自模型自己。

label.en: Active learning is better because pseudo-labels are always accurate
label.zh: 主动学习更好，因为伪标签总是准确的

feedback.en: Active learning uses true labels, not pseudo-labels; and pseudo-labels are not always accurate.
feedback.zh: 主动学习用的是真标签而不是伪标签；而伪标签并不总是准确。

explain.en: Active learning spends the labelling budget; self-training spends none.
explain.zh: 主动学习花标注预算；自训练不花。

title.zh: A 部分：主动学习

prompt.en: Describe the motivation behind active learning, and explain why uncertainty sampling can pick poor instances. (1-3 lines.)
prompt.zh: 说明主动学习背后的动机，并解释不确定性采样为什么可能选到不好的实例。（1-3 行。）

key_points.en: Labels are scarce and expensive; the learner chooses which instances to label to reach accuracy with fewer labels
key_points.zh: 标签稀缺且昂贵；让学习者自己选标哪些实例，以更少标签达到相同准确率

key_points.en: Uncertainty sampling queries instances near the boundary or where the model is unsure
key_points.zh: 不确定性采样查询靠近边界或模型没把握的实例

key_points.en: It can select outliers or noise (uncertain but unrepresentative) and introduces sampling bias
key_points.zh: 它可能选中离群点或噪声（不确定但没有代表性），并带来采样偏差

model_answer.en: Labels are costly, so active learning lets the model choose which unlabelled instances an oracle should label, reaching a given accuracy with fewer labels. Uncertainty sampling queries the most uncertain instances, but these can be outliers or noise, which are uncertain yet unrepresentative, and the chosen set is biased away from the true distribution.
model_answer.zh: Labels are costly, so active learning lets the model choose which unlabelled instances an oracle should label, reaching a given accuracy with fewer labels. Uncertainty sampling queries the most uncertain instances, but these can be outliers or noise, which are uncertain yet unrepresentative, and the chosen set is biased away from the true distribution.

explain.en: Motivation plus one weakness of uncertainty sampling.
explain.zh: 动机，加上不确定性采样的一个弱点。

title.zh: A 部分：自训练

prompt.en: Why can self-training make a classifier worse, and what is the usual safeguard? (1-3 lines.)
prompt.zh: 自训练为什么可能让分类器变差？通常的保护措施是什么？（1-3 行。）

key_points.en: Wrong pseudo-labels are added to L and treated as truth, so errors reinforce (confirmation bias)
key_points.zh: 错误的伪标签被加入 L 并当作真值，错误会被强化（确认偏差）

key_points.en: It needs the assumption that nearby points share labels; if it fails, labels spread wrongly
key_points.zh: 它需要“靠近的点标签相同”的假设；假设不成立时标签会传错

key_points.en: Safeguard: a confidence threshold so only high-confidence predictions join L
key_points.zh: 保护措施：置信度阈值，只让高置信度的预测加入 L

model_answer.en: Self-training adds its own predictions to L as if they were true labels, so any wrong pseudo-label is trained on and reinforced (confirmation bias). It relies on nearby points sharing a label; where this fails the errors spread. A confidence threshold, adding only highly confident predictions, limits the damage.
model_answer.zh: Self-training adds its own predictions to L as if they were true labels, so any wrong pseudo-label is trained on and reinforced (confirmation bias). It relies on nearby points sharing a label; where this fails the errors spread. A confidence threshold, adding only highly confident predictions, limits the damage.

explain.en: The failure (reinforced errors), its condition, and the safeguard.
explain.zh: 失败的原因（错误被强化）、它的条件，以及保护措施。

title.en: Section C: labelling on a budget
title.zh: C 部分：预算有限的标注

prompt.en: You must build a classifier for 20,000 support emails (5 categories). You have 300 labelled emails, 19,700 unlabelled, and an annotator who can label 500 more. Propose a plan: which techniques, in which order, and what could go wrong?
prompt.zh: 你要为 2 万封客服邮件（5 个类别）建一个分类器。有 300 封有标签、19,700 封无标签，还有一位标注员能再标 500 封。提出方案：用哪些技术、按什么顺序、可能出什么问题？

key_points.en: Train on the 300; use active learning (margin or entropy for 5 classes, or QBC) to choose the 500 to label, in batches
key_points.zh: 先用 300 封训练；用主动学习（5 个类用边际或熵，或 QBC）分批挑出 500 封去标注

key_points.en: Optionally self-training with a strict threshold on the rest; hold out labelled data to validate
key_points.zh: 可选：对其余邮件做严格阈值的自训练；留出有标签数据做验证

key_points.en: Risks: outliers/noise queried, sampling bias, confirmation bias, over-confident probabilities
key_points.zh: 风险：查到离群点/噪声、采样偏差、确认偏差、概率过于自信

key_points.en: Mitigation: density weighting, keep a random labelled validation set, check class balance
key_points.zh: 对策：密度加权，保留一份随机抽样的有标签验证集，检查类别平衡

model_answer.en: Train a first model on the 300 labelled emails and spend the 500-label budget with active learning: score the unlabelled pool by margin (or entropy, since there are 5 classes), label the most uncertain batch, retrain, and repeat. Optionally add self-training on very confident predictions with a strict threshold. Risks are queried outliers and noise, sampling bias and confirmation bias, so use density weighting and keep a randomly sampled labelled validation set to measure real accuracy.
model_answer.zh: Train a first model on the 300 labelled emails and spend the 500-label budget with active learning: score the unlabelled pool by margin (or entropy, since there are 5 classes), label the most uncertain batch, retrain, and repeat. Optionally add self-training on very confident predictions with a strict threshold. Risks are queried outliers and noise, sampling bias and confirmation bias, so use density weighting and keep a randomly sampled labelled validation set to measure real accuracy.

explain.en: A design answer orders the techniques and names the risks.
explain.zh: 设计题的答案要排好技术的顺序，并说出风险。

title.zh: 要记住的

rows.en: Why
rows.zh: 为什么

rows.en: labels are scarce and costly; unlabelled data is cheap; unsupervised results are hard to interpret
rows.zh: 标签稀缺且昂贵；无标签数据便宜；无监督的结果难解释

rows.en: Semi-supervised
rows.zh: 半监督

rows.en: learn from $L \cup U$, $|U| \gg |L|$; needs an assumption (smoothness, cluster, manifold)
rows.zh: 从 $L \cup U$ 学习，$|U| \gg |L|$；需要假设（平滑、聚类、流形）

rows.en: Self-training
rows.zh: 自训练

rows.en: train on L, predict U, add high-confidence pseudo-labels, repeat until L is unchanged; threshold = safety net; failure = confirmation bias
rows.zh: 在 L 上训练，预测 U，加入高置信度的伪标签，重复到 L 不变；阈值 = 安全网；失败方式 = 确认偏差

rows.en: Active learning
rows.zh: 主动学习

rows.en: the model asks an oracle for labels of chosen instances; pool-based, stream-based, query synthesis
rows.zh: 模型向专家要自己挑出的实例的标签；基于池、基于流、查询合成

rows.en: Uncertainty sampling
rows.zh: 不确定性采样

rows.en: least confidence: $\min \max_y P$; margin: $\min (P_1 - P_2)$; entropy: $\max -\sum P\log_2 P$. Can disagree with 3+ classes
rows.zh: 最小置信度：$\min \max_y P$；边际：$\min (P_1 - P_2)$；熵：$\max -\sum P\log_2 P$。三个及以上类时可能不一致

rows.en: QBC
rows.zh: 委员会查询

rows.en: committee of models; query the instance with the most disagreement (vote entropy)
rows.zh: 一个模型委员会；查询分歧最大（投票熵最大）的实例

rows.en: Cautions
rows.zh: 注意

rows.en: active learning: sampling bias, outliers/noise; augmentation: label-preserving only, may add unreal features
rows.zh: 主动学习：采样偏差、离群点/噪声；增强：只能做不改变标签的扰动，可能引入不真实的特征

rows.en: Not the same
rows.zh: 别混淆

rows.en: self-training: labels from the model, free but risky; active learning: true labels from a human, costs budget
rows.zh: 自训练：标签来自模型，免费但有风险；主动学习：标签来自人，花预算
